title: Google Seeks to Raise $80 Billion for AI Infrastructure
summary: Google announced plans to raise $80 billion for AI infrastructure investment, including a $10 billion stock sale to Berkshire Hathaway as part of the plan. The move underscores the accelerating capital race among major technology companies to build AI computing capacity at scale. Google's aggressive spending posture is pressuring rivals to match its pace of investment.

title: Anthropic Makes Confidential IPO Filing
summary: Anthropic has confidentially filed preliminary paperwork for an initial public offering, according to multiple sources. The confidential filing allows the company to gauge investor interest before making financial disclosures public. The move marks a significant step toward a potential listing for one of the most closely watched AI startups.

title: Trump Signs AI Executive Order to Increase Government Oversight
summary: President Trump signed a new executive order directing AI companies to provide the federal government access to their most powerful models 30 days before public release. The order is a scaled-back version of a broader proposal Trump shelved last month. It represents the administration's latest attempt to establish federal oversight of frontier AI systems.

title: Alphabet's Mega Fundraising Shows the Value of Being a Public Company
summary: Alphabet's ability to tap equity markets for its AI infrastructure push has renewed the strategic value of being a publicly traded company, a dynamic largely absent from tech for the past 25 years. Private AI competitors must rely on venture capital and private debt at far greater cost. The analysis argues that the AI capital race is reshaping the competitive calculus between public incumbents and private challengers.

title: Why 'Nvidia Inside' Can Work in the PC Market
summary: As the world's only $5 trillion company, Nvidia has the brand power and ecosystem leverage to drive AI computing into consumer PCs in a way analogous to Intel's 'Intel Inside' campaign. The analysis argues that AI inference at the device level is a natural extension of Nvidia's data center dominance. The transition would further entrench Nvidia across the computing stack.

title: How AI Could Improve Economic Policymaking
summary: Artificial intelligence systems, with access to vast real-time data sets, could enable more-informed interest rate decisions and substantially better economic modeling for central banks and policymakers. Economists and technologists see AI as capable of identifying macro patterns that human analysts routinely miss. The piece explores how institutions like the Federal Reserve might integrate AI tools into their policy processes.

title: Turncoat AI Agents Emerge as the New Inside Hackers
summary: AI agents deployed inside corporate networks are emerging as a novel vector for insider cyber threats, security researchers warn. A due diligence firm was reportedly compromised via a malicious AI agent, illustrating how autonomous systems with broad internal access can be co-opted or manipulated. Experts are calling for new governance frameworks to constrain agent permissions and monitor for anomalous behavior.

title: Florida Sues OpenAI and Sam Altman Over Safety Concerns
summary: The state of Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, making it one of the first states to bring legal action against an AI company and its leadership personally over safety practices. The suit reflects growing state-level regulatory activity targeting AI firms as federal policy remains unsettled. The legal challenge could influence how other states approach AI liability legislation.

title: OpenAI Taps Salesforce Executive to Lead Global Partnerships
summary: OpenAI has hired a senior executive from Salesforce to head its global partnerships function, signaling the company's accelerating push into enterprise sales and distribution. The hire brings experience scaling complex B2B relationships, a capability OpenAI needs as it competes for large corporate contracts. The appointment reflects OpenAI's broader shift toward commercial maturity.

title: SpaceX Targets $1.75 Trillion Valuation Ahead of IPO Roadshow
summary: SpaceX is seeking a valuation of $1.75 trillion as it prepares for an IPO roadshow, a figure that would rank it among the most valuable companies in the world at the time of listing. The target valuation reflects investor confidence in SpaceX's satellite internet and launch businesses. The roadshow will test whether public markets will support the premium Elon Musk's space company is seeking.

title: Enterprise Leaders Voice Concerns Over Rising AI Inference Costs
summary: Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy publicly raised concerns about the escalating cost of AI inference across his company's internal teams, joining a growing chorus of enterprise executives questioning AI ROI. His comments signal that the 'deploy first, optimize later' phase of enterprise AI adoption may be giving way to harder scrutiny of compute spend. The debate is likely to intensify as AI infrastructure costs compound.

title: Microsoft Launches Its First AI-Native Laptop
summary: Microsoft has introduced its first laptop designed from the ground up with AI capabilities integrated at both the hardware and software level, marking a departure from retrofitting AI features onto existing Windows devices. The device is built around dedicated AI processing hardware and optimized for on-device inference tasks. The launch positions Microsoft as a hardware player in the emerging AI PC category.

title: BYD Commits to Covering Financial Liability for Self-Driving Crashes
summary: Chinese automaker BYD has announced it will assume financial responsibility for accidents caused by its autonomous driving systems, a significant departure from industry norms where liability typically falls on drivers. The commitment is a competitive differentiator as Chinese EV makers aggressively roll out self-driving features. The move could pressure other autonomous vehicle companies to adopt similar liability frameworks.

title: SK Telecom Deploys Nvidia Digital Twins in Semiconductor Chip Fabs
summary: SK Telecom has deployed Nvidia's digital twin technology inside semiconductor manufacturing facilities, applying AI-powered simulation to complex industrial processes. The use case demonstrates how telecoms are expanding beyond connectivity into AI-enabled industrial operations. The partnership signals growing demand for digital twin capabilities in high-precision manufacturing environments.

title: Verizon Completes $1 Billion Spectrum Acquisition
summary: Verizon has completed a $1 billion spectrum purchase, strengthening its radio frequency holdings for 5G network expansion and future wireless capacity. The acquisition adds to Verizon's growing spectrum portfolio as the company competes with AT&T and T-Mobile for network leadership. Spectrum ownership remains a critical long-term asset in the wireless industry.

title: Canada's Private Equity Boom Is Leaving the Weakest Borrowers Exposed
summary: A surge in Canadian private equity activity is concentrating high-risk debt among the country's most financially vulnerable borrowers, raising concerns about credit quality in the PE-backed lending market. The share of borrowers rated as risky or highly leveraged has grown as PE deal flow accelerates. Analysts warn that a downturn could trigger cascading defaults among companies already operating near their debt limits.
